subtle-from-hue.says: A soft fill comes from the hue of its own color: the same hue scale as its @.

hover-from-fill.says: A hover is the hue of its fill, one step on.

grays-from-neutral.says: Surfaces, lines, page text, the secondary action and disabled read only steps of the neutral ramp.

fill-text-from-tone.says: The text on a fill is the text its fill's tone picks: on-light or on-dark.

selection-from-brand.says: Selection takes the hue of the main action, so a selected item reads as the brand's.

scrim-from-black.says: The scrim is the scheme's black, see-through, so it dims the page in both modes.

fill-pairs-with-text.says: Every fill pairs with the text on it, by tone, and the pair keeps its contrast floor. A step number makes a promise: steps 400 apart give 3:1, 500 apart give 4.5:1, 700 apart give 7:1, in every hue of a scheme.

category-apart-from-status.says: A category color has no meaning, so it never takes a status hue: a category in the warning hue reads as a warning.

danger-apart-from-primary.says: the primary and danger fills stay at least 10 apart (ΔE in OKLab, ×100) in every brand and mode

surface-ladder.says: In dark mode the surfaces lighten as they rise: sunken, then default, then raised, then floating.

border-width.default.why: We use a 1px default line for dividers and card borders in order to give separation between rows. A thin stroke does this by breaking the surface with the least weight a line can have; as a divider it decorates, so it has no contrast floor. So rows and cards stay apart without taking room from the data, because lines separate groups (elevation.definition) and AA is the floor (accessibility.definition).

motion.duration.feedback.why: We use 120ms (fast) for hover, press and toggle feedback in order to confirm each action inside the productive limit of 150ms. The duration does this by ending the change before the eye leaves the control. So experts see each action land and never wait for it, because motion is for feedback only, which makes the family productive (motion.roles), and feedback feels fast (motion.values).

So experts open a menu many times a shift and never wait for it, because the family is productive (motion.roles) and there is one speed (motion.count).
